findings.title: Finite-height first-order localization without compact support
findings.assertion_status: The literal estimate (1.12) is false in its stated signed-background class.
findings.hypotheses: d=1,s=0,N=2; fixed smooth bounded v with plateaus -1,0,+1 and compactly supported derivative; Omega=[-3,3], ell=3; particles R+-1/4, R>10; mu=p_R+q_j has mass one, global and local Linfinity norm 8, compact support and finite absolute logarithmic energy; lambda=1/16; #I_Omega=0; r_i=1/64.
findings.decisive_evidence: The q_j single-layer gradient tends to zero in global L2 by a low/high Fourier split. The limiting commutator is 4 log((2R+1/2)/(2R-1/2)) ~ 2/R, but the local slab energy is at most 144/(R-13/4)^2. No universal constant works as j->infinity and then R->infinity.
findings.counterevidence: Compactly supported v or nonnegative-only mu would exclude this example. The theorem explicitly permits signed mu. Full vertical integration avoids this finite-height counterexample.
findings.core_dependency: Local cutoff support and the statement (1.12), not the global first-order bound.
findings.repair_boundary: Amend support/domain hypotheses or retain full vertical integration and recheck the proof. No complete replacement theorem or failure of the compact-field high-order or mean-field statements is claimed.

findings.title: Missing acceleration term in fixed-velocity transport hierarchy
source_locators: Lemma A.7 and Proposition A.1, pp.67-69
findings.assertion_status: The identity (A.7) and its use in the alternative proof are invalid.
findings.hypotheses: d=3,s=1,k=0; smooth compact v equals x near e1; a real annular-Fourier Schwartz potential h has partial_1 h(e1)=-2; f=-Delta h/(4pi) is zero-mean Schwartz with Fourier support away from zero. A separate radial-bump illustration checks exact scalar derivatives.
findings.decisive_evidence: The chain rule adds m integral D^m g:[(v dot grad)v tensor (v(x)-v(y))^(m-1)]. For m=1 this equals -2 at e1,t=0. The radial-bump arithmetic gives dt kappa1=-4, v dot grad kappa1=2, kappa2=0.
findings.counterevidence: A time-dependent Eulerian velocity v_t=v composed with (I+t v)^-1 gives a different possible hierarchy. The source explicitly fixes v in A.6. Section 4 has a separate PDE route.
findings.core_dependency: Lemma A.3 -> Lemma A.5 -> Lemma A.7 -> the alternative proof of Proposition A.1.
findings.repair_boundary: Redefine the hierarchy and redo its induction or retain the missing terms. The estimate and principal theorems are not disproved by this proof failure.

findings.title: Unsmeared singularities and logarithmic cell energy in local renormalization
source_locators: Lemma 5.1 (5.7), p.51; closing use of (2.30), p.52
findings.assertion_status: Both (5.7) on its displayed domain and the p=0 logarithmic case of (5.40) are false.
findings.hypotheses: Example A: d=1,s=0,N=2, mu=1_{[-1/2,1/2]}, particles 0,4, v supported [-1,1], Omega'=[-3,3], Omega=[-18,18], ell=3, lambda=1/2. Example B: d=2,s=0,N=2, particles 0,e1, mu_R=nu0/4+nu_Re1/4+nu_3Re1/2 with uniform disks radius 1/10, R>50; Omega and Omega' are closed balls; local density and radii fixed; genuine radial moment-cancelling mollifier; cell radius 2R has mass 1/2. Both backgrounds are nonnegative.
findings.decisive_evidence: A: the unsmeared particle at 4 lies in the integration slab, giving (pi/2)log(epsilon0/epsilon)+O(1) energy while Xi is finite. B: the neutral cell has exactly E0+(1/8)log R logarithmic interaction energy and 2pi E0+(pi/4)log R Dirichlet energy, contradicting C/N^2 for fixed eta.
findings.counterevidence: The needed local cell norm can remain bounded; the proof replaces it by a global norm. The global Section 5.4 estimate uses a different Term 2 bound. Signed backgrounds create further total-variation issues, but the two counterexamples do not depend on signed backgrounds.
findings.core_dependency: Smeared Term 1 and local regularity estimate of Term 2 in the high-order renormalization.
findings.repair_boundary: Avoid unsmeared singularities in the energy domain, keep a valid local cell bound, and account for total variation. No counterexample to the intended higher-order final theorem is claimed.

findings.title: Nonmonotone mesoscale truncation path
findings.assertion_status: The claimed monotonicity in the proof is false, including after the fixed-potential typo is repaired.
findings.hypotheses: d=3,s=1,N=2; Omega upper half-space; particles at (0,0,3lambda) and (3lambda,0,3lambda); 0<lambda<1; bounded probability background far from the particle balls within Omega with height 1/(2lambda^3); radii path lambda,2lambda,lambda/4.
findings.decisive_evidence: The two radius-2lambda shells at separation 3lambda have mutual energy 5/(16lambda), versus 1/(3lambda) at either nonoverlapping radius. Thus F_eta2-F_eta1=1/(192lambda)>0. Literal (2.45) freezes h_N,r and also fails monotonicity. The separate derivative inequality has -100 >= -25/4, which is false.
findings.counterevidence: The selected pair sum in (2.40) may be empty for this proof-step counterexample, so it does not refute the proposition's final estimate. The derivative sign issue alone is repairable with a constant.
findings.core_dependency: Mesoscale proposition used in local and macroscopic renormalization estimates.
findings.repair_boundary: Rebuild an admissible truncation comparison or control reset terms and vertical tails. No complete repaired proof is certified.

findings.title: Undefined indices and unrecovered high-order derivative budget
findings.assertion_status: The printed formula has unbound indices; the supplied proof does not deliver the stated C^{2n-1,1} derivative budget.
findings.hypotheses: n>=2; fixed compact support, fixed admissible lambda and ell; smooth approximating fields v_J=v0+J^(-2n) chi sin(Jx), with nonzero v0'' on the cutoff plateau.
findings.decisive_evidence: At n=3,p=2 the lambda exponent uses c2 while only c1 is bound. Relabelling a_i to b_i=1+a_i in (5.42) gives sum b_i<=3n-p, not 2n, and the term p=n-1,a1=2n requires D^(2n+1)v. Its norm grows like J while C^{2n-1,1} stays bounded.
findings.counterevidence: A sharper local regularity proof could improve the derivative count; the sequence is not a counterexample to the best possible corrected final estimate. The empty product is at p=n, not the printed p=0.
findings.core_dependency: Regularity induction -> Term 2 bound -> final claimed (1.13).
findings.repair_boundary: Supply sharper estimates or state a weaker bound with the actual derivative budget; index repair alone is insufficient.

findings.title: False uniform amplitude dependence in Corollary 1.3, with local norm-power subfindings
findings.assertion_status: The uniform linear dependence on M in the high-order corollary is false; related norm powers are local typographical/algebraic errors.
findings.hypotheses: d=1,s=0,N=2; mu=1 on [-1/2,1/2]; particles +-1/4; compact v_A=A v0, v0=x on [-2,2] and supported [-4,4]; ell=6, Omega'=B6, Omega=B36, lambda=1/2.
findings.decisive_evidence: The n=2 integral is -A^2/2 and its absolute value A^2/2, while M=A M0 and the energy bracket is independent of A. Squared commutator norms require degree 2n; the fractional duality exponent must be (d-s)/2.
findings.counterevidence: The consistent unsquared estimate (3.17) supports a local correction. Allowing the constant to depend on M changes the uniform corollary.
findings.core_dependency: The source p5 presents Corollary1.3 as the precise scale/homogeneity consequence of Theorem1.2(1.13). The p6 uniform estimate fails on an admissible n=2 affine-support example: A^2/2 versus a bound linear in M=A M0.
findings.repair_boundary: Replace M by M^n and restore squared powers and the correct fractional duality exponent. This does not repair the other higher-order proof issues.
findings.severity_reason: Demonstrated failure of a stated central quantitative guarantee. An elementary M^n repair does not justify downgrading that failure. Separate explanatory squared-norm and duality slips remain local Minor subfindings.

findings.title: Missing diagonal self-interaction term
findings.assertion_status: The claimed decomposition omits surviving smooth-atomic diagonal terms.
findings.hypotheses: Use the P06 compact affine logarithmic example with n=2,A=1 and unit-mass, possibly signed, mollifiers with the prescribed small supports.
findings.decisive_evidence: K2=1; Term1=Term2=Term4=0 but Term3=-1/2. Exact expansion adds N^-2 sum_i[int K rho_i rho_i -2 int K(x_i,y)rho_i(y)dy].
findings.counterevidence: The missing terms obey C||grad v||^n/(N^2 eta_i^s) per particle; the logarithmic case is directly controlled by the density error. Thus the equality's failure does not imply failure of the final estimate.
findings.core_dependency: Term 3 renormalization, including its reused global form.
findings.repair_boundary: Insert the exact self correction and bound it with fixed total-variation constants and the existing self-energy/density budget.

findings.title: Moment-cancelling mollifier construction has a nonzero second moment
findings.assertion_status: The construction fails for the stated unrestricted smooth unit-mass bumps.
findings.hypotheses: d=1,m=2; Fourier convention exp(-i xi x); psi,zeta are smooth compact unit-mass bumps with first moments A,B, e.g. translates by 1 of centered even probability bumps.
findings.decisive_evidence: The printed formula yields rhohat=1+AB xi^2+O(xi^3), so the second moment is -2AB; A=B=1 gives -2.
findings.counterevidence: Centered symmetric bumps avoid this second-order cross term. A Taylor quotient construction works at every order.
findings.core_dependency: Moment cancellation in the far-particle Taylor remainder.
findings.repair_boundary: Use P=Taylor_m[(psihat-1)/zetahat] and rhohat=psihat-zetahat P; retain signed-mollifier total-variation constants. This is a local repair, not a proof of all surrounding bounds.
